races.name: Ire-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
BetVictor EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Apple Print & Creative Rose Bowl Stakes (Listed Race)
BetVictor Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Name The Day
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in this field, holding a course-and-distance profile over shorter trips and stepping up to 1m; Eve Johnson Houghton in solid 14-day form (7/29) and Charles Bishop has the mandate to bowl along, but racing out of the lead (STYLE_FIT 0.93) tempers confidence in this specific role — the real question is whether the mile stretches stamina after a 14-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Areti
runners_data.note: William Buick booking for Oliver Cole is the standout trainer–jockey angle here; dual-placed form at 7-8f on good and standard gives solid profile for this trip, and with a versatile unknown style she can be positioned to suit if Buick elects to track the pace through the first half.

runners_data.name: Pierpoint
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon yard sends a genuine hold-up horse over a trip shorter than the 9-10f he has been tried at recently; Pat Dobbs will need plenty to go right from out wide, and the step back in distance after struggling in soft is a question mark, though good ground suits.

runners_data.name: Rajiba
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes over on a filly with consistent placed form at 6-8f, all on standard or similar going; an unknown style gives Murphy maximum tactical latitude, and the freshness off a 15-day break looks positive with this trip firmly within her range.

runners_data.name: Luminare
runners_data.note: William Haggas hold-up specialist with a win and multiple places at 7-8f, including two runs on good ground where she has produced strong finishes; Tom Marquand will be looking for a strong enough gallop to make ground, and at 36 days since her last run she arrives with time on her side.

runners_data.name: Accademia
runners_data.note: Kieran Shoemark rides a hold-up filly who landed a 7f win on good ground 14 days ago — the recency and going are both positive; Ed Walker's yard is 7/39 in the 14-day window, and a step up to 1m is the main unknown after all career runs have been over shorter.

runners_data.name: Starlight Sami
runners_data.note: Denis Coakley's filly is a true closer by profile, though the map has her in midfield because the hold-up contingent is too large for all to sit deep; her Goodwood win came over 7f on good and her form reads well for this going, but if she cannot get back to her natural position, the style compromise (STYLE_FIT 0.92) is real.

runners_data.name: Lightning Glory
runners_data.note: Simon & Ed Crisford's prominent racer has placed form at 8f on standard surfaces; Rossa Ryan will likely attempt to sit second behind Name The Day, which gives her a clean passage, and consistent recent finishes make her a reliable shaper even if a career win at this level has not yet materialised.

runners_data.name: Majd Al Kazem
runners_data.note: A very long 268-day absence is the dominant note here — all the tactical redistribution context aside, returning off nearly nine months is a huge ask in a competitive handicap, and Hilal Kobeissi's yard is 0/1 in the 14-day window; his true hold-up style being mapped to midfield (STYLE_FIT 0.90) is a secondary concern behind the fitness question.

runners_data.name: Berlinetta
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's hold-up filly returns after 172 days off, stepping up markedly in trip from 5-6f to 1m for the first time; Connor Beasley takes the ride but the combination of an extended break, a career-longest trip, and being pushed out of her natural deep position (STYLE_FIT 0.90) stacks the concerns.

races.paceDynamic: Name The Day is the sole confirmed front-runner in this ten-runner mile handicap and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should be allowed to bowl along at a sustainable, self-set tempo without being pressured into burning excessive early energy. Lightning Glory will likely sit second or third from a prominent position, giving the race a clear shape: controlled pace in front, a chasing pack strung behind. That uncontested, measured gallop strongly favours horses who can travel just off the pace and produce a clean turn-of-foot in the straight — a prominent-to-midfield profile is best placed, while genuine hold-up horses will need an above-average end-to-end pace to generate the gaps they rely on. The field holds more true hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear: Starlight Sami, Majd Al Kazem, and Berlinetta are all genuine closers who are unlikely to secure their preferred deep position and will be shuffled into midfield roles that compromise their natural strengths.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Rails Run
scenarios.trigger: If Name The Day dictates a modest uncontested tempo and prominent/mid-division horses land the clearest run up the Newbury straight.
scenarios.body: Name The Day sets a comfortable rhythm, the field settles in a compact bunch, and those tracking within three or four lengths off the pace get first run in the straight with the best sectionals still to come. Horses able to sit handy, travel kindly, and quicken on good ground are squarely in the money-zone here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Name The Day and Lightning Glory kick clear at the two-furlong pole and force the hold-up horses to cover too much ground.
scenarios.body: A steady early gallop followed by a sustained two-furlong drive from Name The Day and Lightning Glory punishes anything stuck wide or deep; they empty the tank of those attempting to close from the rear. Front-end stamina and tactical speed at the mile trip are rewarded, and those who tracked in the first half-dozen are best placed to pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply from halfway and opens up enough of a gap for hold-up horses to make meaningful late progress.
scenarios.body: A stronger-than-expected pace — possibly if Lightning Glory pushes Name The Day harder than anticipated — could string the field out and create room for true closers late on. However, with Starlight Sami, Majd Al Kazem, and Berlinetta all mapped away from their natural back positions, genuine closers are structurally compromised and this scenario carries limited probability as a result.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Wide Draws Win
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses contest the early lead, creating a messy pace and unsettling the field's settling patterns.
scenarios.body: Any scramble for position from the break would accelerate the early fractions, compress the field mid-race, and hand an advantage to a horse wide enough to avoid the resulting traffic as rivals tire. This is the least likely shape given Name The Day's clear front-running mandate and the absence of any other confirmed pace-maker.

watchPoints.text: Name The Day sets the only confirmed lead — watch whether Charles Bishop allows an honest pace or dawdles, as any slow-down in the first three furlongs risks turning this into a sprint finish that negates her positional advantage.
Majd Al Kazem has not run for 268 days; if fitness is lacking, he could drop out quickly from midfield and cause traffic issues for the horses immediately behind him in the straight.

Starlight Sami, Majd Al Kazem, and Berlinetta are all true closers mapped into midfield — if they bunch together on the inner approaching the two-furlong pole, a significant pocket of traffic is possible that could block the runs of legitimate hold-up horses like Luminare and Accademia.

William Buick's positioning of Areti in the early stages is worth monitoring — if he elects to track Name The Day's back in the first three, Areti's tactical profile could be the hinge point that determines whether Scenario A or B plays out.

Berlinetta is making her seasonal reappearance after 172 days and tackles a career-longest trip; how she handles the early pace in unfamiliar mid-division territory will signal whether she is ready to play a role or simply a fitness run.

races.name: Uhy Ross Brooke Fillies' Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Aphrodite Spirit
runners_data.note: Roger Teal's four-year-old has placed at this trip on good ground before and is proven over 10f on similar going; she races prominently and should slot into second or third here, which suits the likely shape, though 46 days off is worth noting with a 0/10 trainer run record in that window.

runners_data.name: Green Sky
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's six-year-old carries strong recent form — two wins from the last two starts over 12f on good — but is a genuine hold-up horse who needs others to burn petrol in front; Oisin Murphy's presence is a major positive but a pedestrian pace is a significant threat to his chance, and his trip form at 19f-plus was poor.

runners_data.name: Koala Rose
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old is the confirmed pace-setter here with a high STYLE_FIT flag indicating she is operating slightly out of her most comfortable role; she has placed consistently on good ground over longer trips and with no rival to press her early, she holds a strong positional advantage, though her form shows no wins yet.

runners_data.name: Kelly Burn
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's three-year-old boasts a win over 14f on good ground and has the form to be competitive; at heart a prominent racer, she finds herself unable to claim that position here with Koala Rose already there — she is most likely to track the leader closely, and if she can execute that role cleanly, her recent winning form makes her dangerous.

races.paceDynamic: Koala Rose is the confirmed front-runner in this four-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she should settle into an uncontested, controlled gallop from the outset over 1m5½f at Newbury. The pace is likely to be measured rather than searching, meaning stamina will be tested less than tactical position and the ability to sustain a long-distance kick. Green Sky is the only true hold-up type and will be ridden from the rear by Oisin Murphy, likely needing a genuinely strong pace to reel in the leader — which this field may not generate. Kelly Burn is a natural prominent racer who has been redistributed to midfield on the map because Koala Rose has already claimed the lead role; her true preference is to race close to the pace, and she is most likely to track Koala Rose in second rather than settle away from the action. This shape — a lone front-runner dictating a modest, unchallenged gallop — strongly favours horses that can hold a tracking position and produce a sustained finish, rather than those relying on a strong pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Koala Rose Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Koala Rose bowls along in front at her own pace and no rival applies early pressure to raise the tempo.
scenarios.body: Koala Rose sets a comfortable, controlled gallop that takes the sting out of closers, and any rival with the tactical speed to track her and produce a clean kick home is ideally placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Kelly Burn or Aphrodite Spirit track Koala Rose at close quarters and produce a superior finish in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: The pace stays modest but a tracking rival conserves energy perfectly and has enough in reserve to collar Koala Rose inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Aids Closer
scenarios.trigger: If Kelly Burn pushes up and creates a contested pace, elevating the tempo enough for Green Sky to close from the rear.
scenarios.body: A faster early gallop stretches the field and drains the front-runners, leaving the freshest Green Sky — ridden with patience by Murphy — to swoop late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Tactical Affair
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls at walking pace and the race degenerates into a sprint finish with no clear tactical advantage for any runner.
scenarios.body: With such a small field and no pressure applied, the race could become a lottery decided by raw ability in the final two furlongs rather than race shape.

watchPoints.text: Koala Rose has no rivals willing to press her for the lead — watch whether she slows the pace to a crawl, as that makes the closing stages unpredictable and opens the door for Aphrodite Spirit or Kelly Burn to produce a sharp late kick.

Kelly Burn's redistribution from prominent to midfield is a key tactical watch: if Saffie Osborne aggressively pushes forward to chase Koala Rose early, she could revert to her natural position and stretch the field, which changes the entire race shape.

Green Sky's last run was just seven days ago over 12f — watch his early behaviour and whether Murphy settles him immediately at the rear, as any keenness from a fresh horse in a small field could compromise his patient hold-up plan.

With only four runners, gaps in the field may open easily on the straight Newbury track — watch how quickly the field strings out, as any runner who drifts wide or loses momentum at a crucial point faces a very difficult task to recover in such a small, tactical race.

races.name: Crossland Employment Solicitors Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Cloth Of Gold
runners_data.note: Has winning form over 10f on good and standard going but goes here stepped up to 1m3f; Charlie Johnston's yard is in good form (8/67 over 14 days) and the light 13-day turnaround suggests confidence, though similar-going form reads just 2/8 with no wins at this trip, which is a genuine query.

runners_data.name: Nap Hand
runners_data.note: A thorough stayer whose five-run historical sample shows consistent placings at 12f-17f on good ground, logging 7 place efforts from 10 runs at similar going; Chris Gordon has no 14-day runners logged, and at 19 days fresh this six-year-old needs the pace to truly flow to unleash his staying kick.

runners_data.name: Magnatura
runners_data.note: In-form with a recent win and placed efforts over 7-8f, but today's step up to 1m3f is a significant stamina test for a horse whose entire form base sits at sprint-to-mile trips; he is a natural front-runner by profile who will find himself shuffled back by the race shape here, adding a further layer of doubt to an already uncertain trip test.

runners_data.name: Turty Tree
runners_data.note: Fitted with a hood and trained by Andrew Balding (11/56 in 14 days), he arrives having won over 10f on good going last time and placed at 12f, suggesting the step to 1m3f is well within range; Murphy's tactical intelligence in a small field makes him the most likely beneficiary of a tracking role directly behind Cloth Of Gold.

runners_data.name: Devil's Peak
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden send out this three-year-old in a hood 35 days after his last run, with a five-run history showing consistent place efforts but no wins; Buick will look to employ a patient, hold-up strategy but the lack of genuine pace in this race means the closer's ground may simply not materialise.

races.paceDynamic: Cloth Of Gold is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only five runners and no genuine pace rival to push him, he should be allowed to roll along at a comfortable, self-regulated gallop from the off. Turty Tree and Magnatura are both naturally prominent types who will want to sit close to the pace, but with Cloth Of Gold likely dictating cheaply, one of them will inevitably be shuffled back further than ideal — Turty Three, with Oisin Murphy in the saddle and the better record over this trip, is most likely to secure the second position ahead of Magnatura. This field holds more prominent/front-running types than can all get their preferred berth, meaning Magnatura is mapped to midfield despite being a natural forwardly-placed racer. The controlled, unhurried pace that Cloth Of Gold can set over 1m3f on good ground sets this race up squarely for a prominent racer able to travel close to the leader and strike decisively, rather than for horses forced to make up ground from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cloth Of Gold Leads Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Cloth Of Gold dictates a steady-to-fair tempo and the race develops into a test of finishing quality from the front.
scenarios.body: Cloth Of Gold controls fractions on the good ground, with Turty Tree tracking closely and able to pounce entering the straight; the unhurried tempo suits horses who can sustain a run rather than those who need a truly searching gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Quickens Past
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is moderate enough that a prominent tracker gets a dream tow and produces a sharp finishing burst.
scenarios.body: Turty Tree or Magnatura, sitting close to Cloth Of Gold throughout, times the run to perfection as the leader's reserves empty in the final furlong; the lack of a searching gallop rewards horses with a sharp change of gear rather than relentless stayers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and leave the closers with daylight to finish past tired rivals.
scenarios.body: Nap Hand or Devil's Peak, given a clear run on the outside from the two-furlong pole, picks up the pieces if Cloth Of Gold has been pressured into a faster-than-expected gallop; both hold-up types have the stamina credentials for 1m3f but depend heavily on the pace being genuinely above a canter.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Turns Tactical Mess
scenarios.trigger: If Turty Tree or Magnatura challenges Cloth Of Gold early and the race collapses into a sprint finish from a crawl.
scenarios.body: A bunched finish from a very slow pace would theoretically open the door to any of the five, but Cloth Of Gold's front-running habit should prevent a true crawl; this scenario requires significant jockey error or a race incident to materialise.

watchPoints.text: Magnatura's true trip stamina is completely unproven — watch whether Kieran Shoemark allows him to settle or burns unnecessary energy fighting for a position he cannot realistically hold in this race shape.
Cloth Of Gold's form over 1m3f is absent from his record; if he ties up in the final two furlongs after setting his own pace, Turty Tree is best placed to pounce immediately.

Nap Hand and Devil's Peak both require a searching gallop to produce their best, and with Cloth Of Gold dictating, watch whether either jockey (Bishop, Buick) switches the angle of attack by making an early move to inject pace themselves.

The going is listed as unknown at Newbury — any overnight rain softening the ground would aid the stayers (Nap Hand) and potentially blunt Cloth Of Gold's front-running effectiveness, shifting probabilities toward the hold-up runners.
